text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a cabinet meeting headed by Prime Minister Ganzouri says that new petroleum fields were discovered in Sinai and Port Said, strategic reserves of all goods is plentiful and three industrial areas will be set up in southern Sohag province. Cabinet approves the prospecting for crude in six concessions.
- President Mubarak and President Arafat dicuss the latest developments in the Middle East peace process.
- Mubarak and Spanish King Juan Carlos discuss bilateral ties between Egypt and Spain.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa does not rule out a meeting between Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.
- Egypt's budget for 1997/8 estimated at 85 billion pounds ($24.99 billion).
- Capital Market Authority to draft new law which will prevent speculation on the bourse and increase flow of investments to Egypt.
- Egypt and Spain to set up joint projects in the new valley and in the Red Sea resort town of Hurghada.
- Public workers paid taxes worth 55 million pounds in the taxes during the past financial year.
- Moslem and Christian leaders hold a demonstration to condemn the terrorist actions in Abu Qurqas where 10 Coptic Christians were killed.
- Cabinet says in a meeting chaired by Ganzouri: Egyptian security does not diffrentiate between a Moslem or a Christian. Efforts to capture terrorists intensified.
- World Bank and International Monetary Fund agree to give technical support to Egypt.
